correctness.rationale: Partial admissible Gram sets contain at most two elements because the Cayley graph is complete bipartite; their positivity is exactly real reflection values of magnitude at most one. The GNS coefficient decomposition on the abelian subgroup proves the Fourier l1 bound. The explicit character/block-state construction proves sufficiency at and below the sharp boundary. The one-negative example and small-group cases follow from exact Fourier coefficients. Finite diagnostics verify sample full positive-type Gram matrices but are not the general proof.

value.rationale: The result classifies a whole natural family of finite-group partial positive-type extension problems with an exact and computable Fourier l1 criterion, explicit positive-state realizations, and sharp smallest-order obstruction. The local condition is the full hypercube; global positivity has a genuinely different geometry. This yields a structural boundary for generalized dihedral groups and an exact geometric S3 corollary, without requiring a generalization to arbitrary operator-valued data.
